challenge.better_approach: Considered requiring equality. The 7 tester red tickets need bounds.in to be the wider one, so the check is containment only.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That paths are compared as written. A './' prefix or a backslash would mismatch. No ticket was measured carrying one, but none was looked for.
challenge.prior_art: bounds is checked only for its shape at _shape_lacks:2500. Grepped tickets/ and questions/ for 'not in bounds.in': nothing.
challenge.real_collision: judge_plan and plan_migration call _shape_lacks, so a judged or migrated plan that writes outside its bounds is now refused too. That is intended; T2 backfills the 2 open tickets that do.

answers.falsifier: Done when a cast writing outside bounds.in is refused by path and a wider bounds.in casts. Wrong if some legitimate class of ticket must write outside its bounds.
answers.how: In transitions._shape_lacks, once bounds is well-shaped, every decisions[i].writes_to and outcomes[i].writes_to path not in bounds.in is a lack naming the path. A comment records why containment runs one way. SKILL.md:204 is reworded. Tooth 6 goes in the prose-plan proof.
answers.traces_to: Law 4: the bounds rule was prose in SKILL.md, and 20 tickets broke it with no red.
answers.what: The cast door refuses a ticket whose decisions or outcomes write to a path its bounds.in does not hold, while still allowing bounds.in to hold more than the writes.

bullets.text: 20 of 480 bounded tickets wrote outside bounds.in with no red
